Éric Dupond-Moretti: French-Italian politician and lawyer (born 1961)
Who among these was born first?
Soichiro Honda (born 1906) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
Which of these four began earliest?
Messerschmitt Bf 109 (founded 1937) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was established earliest?
C (programming language) (founded 1972) is the earliest of the four. C is a general-purpose programming language created in the 1970s by Dennis Ritchie.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
Max Born is a physicist. During World War I, Born was originally placed as a radio operator, but his specialist knowledge led to his being moved to research duties on sound ranging.
Pick the chemist from these four.
Antoine Lavoisier is a chemist. It is generally accepted that Lavoisier's great accomplishments in chemistry stem largely from his changing the science from a qualitative to a quantitative one.
What is the atomic number of Oxygen?
Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.
In what year was Werner Heisenberg born?
Werner Heisenberg: Heisenberg published his Umdeutung paper in 1925, a major reinterpretation of old quantum theory.
In what year was Glutathione discovered?
Glutathione (GSH,) is a tripeptide made of the amino acids glutamate, cysteine, and glycine.
In what year was Morphine discovered?
Morphine, formerly known as morphium, is an opiate found naturally in opium, a dark brown resin produced by drying the latex of opium poppies (Papaver somniferum).
Acetylcysteine: Pfizer. It has been used to treat lactobezoar in infants.
In which country is Embraer E-Jet family based?
Embraer E-Jet family: Brazil. The E-Jet was designed to complement Embraer's earlier ERJ family, the company's first jet-powered regional aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Radon?
Radon: Friedrich Ernst Dorn. Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
Who is credited with discovering Tautavel Man?
Tautavel Man: Henry de Lumley. Tautavel Man refers to the archaic humans which—from approximately 550,000 to 400,000 years ago—inhabited the Caune de l’Arago, a limestone cave in Tautavel, France.
Who is credited with discovering MDMA?
MDMA: Anton Köllisch. MDMA was first synthesized in 1912 by Merck chemist Anton Köllisch.
Though the word is often dropped from its name, invasive ductal carcinoma — the most common breast cancer — technically falls under this broader glandular cancer classification — what is it?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
Adenocarcinoma (AC) is a type of cancer made of cells from glands.
Formed naturally around volcanic vents and on burning coal dumps, this soluble white crystalline salt serves as both a fertilizer and a food additive — what's the compound with formula NH4Cl?
Ammonium chloride is an inorganic chemical compound with the chemical formula NH4Cl, also written as Cl.

This superfamily of tailless Old World primates, native to sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia and more closely related to Old World monkeys than New World ones, includes humans among its members — what's this group called?
Ape (hominoids), are a superfamily of Old World simians native to sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia.
Found throughout North America from Canada to northern Mexico, this sea eagle has two subspecies and forms a pair with the white-tailed eagle—name it.
Bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) is a bird of prey found in North America.

Found mainly in New Guinea, which family of forty-four species — the males famous for extravagant, elaborate plumage sprouting from their beaks, wings, tails, or heads — is confined largely to dense rainforest?
Bird-of-paradise are members of the family Paradisaeidae of the order Passeriformes.
This cabbage-family vegetable, whose large dark-green flowering head is eaten as food, closely resembles its paler relative cauliflower — name it?
Native to nearly all of South America, this semiaquatic, grass-munching cousin of the guinea pig holds the title of largest living rodent — what is it?
Capybara (Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris) is the largest living rodent, native to all countries in South America except Chile.

The smallest recognized dog breed in the world, this Mexican toy breed has large erect ears and a rounded skull, and its genes carry a trace of pre-Columbian indigenous American dog ancestry — which breed?

Chihuahua (dog breed) is a Mexican breed of toy dog and the smallest recognized dog breed in the world. It is primarily kept as a companion animal and is characterized by its compact size, large erect ears, and rounded skull.
This digestive condition refers to swelling or inflammation of the large intestine, and can be acute and short-lived or a long-term, chronic issue — what is it called?
Colitis is swelling or inflammation of the large intestine (colon). It broadly fits into the category of digestive diseases.
Together with birds, this order of predatory reptiles is one of only two survivors of the ancient Archosauria — and it lumps together alligators, caimans, and gharials. What is it?
Crocodilia is an order of semiaquatic, predatory reptiles that are known as crocodilians.
A colorless liquid that's a workhorse solvent for chemical reactions, this compound is officially odorless — yet degraded samples reek of fish thanks to a dimethylamine impurity; what is it?
Dimethylformamide is an organic compound with the chemical formula HCON(CH3)2.

This scientific and engineering discipline uses transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits to control and amplify the flow of electric current, converting between forms like AC to DC. What is the field called?

Electronics is a scientific and engineering discipline that studies and applies the principles of physics to design, create, and operate devices that manipulate electrons and other electrically charged particles.
They're a tiny minority by headcount among living things, yet their larger bodies make their combined biomass dwarf that of bacteria and archaea — what membrane-bound-nucleus group is this?
Eukaryote are the domain Eukaryota or Eukarya, organisms whose cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.
Systematically named methanal and carrying the formula CH2O, this pungent gas turns up in particle board, disinfectants, and lab specimen jars — what is it?

Formaldehyde (for-, US also fr-) (systematic name methanal) is a pungent colorless gas mainly used in the production of industrial resins, such as for particle board, coatings, plastics, pulp, paper, synthetic fibers, and textiles.
The tallest living land animal and the largest ruminant on Earth, this African mammal's closest living relative is the shorter-necked okapi — name the animal?
Giraffe (genus Giraffa) are large African hoofed mammals.
Named for a flattened, laterally extended head shape called a cephalofoil, with eyes placed at each end of the T, this family of sharks includes species mostly grouped in one genus — which sharks?

Hammerhead shark are a group of sharks that form the family Sphyrnidae, named for the unusual and distinctive form of their heads, which are flattened and laterally extended into a cephalofoil (a T-shape or "hammer").
This perennial root vegetable, a relative of mustard, wasabi, broccoli, and cabbage, is grated and used worldwide as a pungent spice and condiment — what plant is it?
This contagious bacterial skin infection most often shows up as yellowish crusts on a child's face, arms, or legs, and spreads easily in crowded day cares and contact sports — what is it?
Impetigo is a contagious bacterial infection that involves the superficial skin.
Director of Columbia's Center for Sustainable Development, which economist led the United Nations Millennium Project's work on the Millennium Development Goals?
Jeffrey Sachs (SAKS; born November 5, 1954) is an American economist and public policy analyst.
Native to Central and South American rainforests, this frugivorous nocturnal mammal related to raccoons and coatis shares its 'honey bear' nickname with an unrelated species — which animal?
Kinkajou (/kkdu/; Potos flavus) is a mammal of the family Procyonidae, a relative to olingos, coatis, raccoons, and the ringtail and cacomistle.
An indoor watchdog by tradition, this dog breed originated high in Tibet — which non-sporting breed is it?
Lhasa Apso is a non-sporting dog breed originating in Tibet.
Caused by a compromised lymphatic system, this condition raises infection risk in affected tissue and is treated with compression and massage rather than water pills — what is it?
Lymphedema (USA), lymphoedema (UK) also known as lymphatic edema (US)/oedema (UK), is a condition of localized swelling caused by a compromised lymphatic system.
This German-British theoretical physicist won a Nobel Prize for his statistical interpretation of the wavefunction, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics. Who is he?
Max Born (11 December 1882 - 5 January 1970) was a German-British theoretical physicist who was instrumental in the development of quantum mechanics.
This unit of time, normally equal to 60 seconds, can rarely stretch to 61 seconds under the UTC time standard because of a leap second — what is it?
Minute (symbol: min) is a unit of time defined as equal to 60 seconds.
Found from Africa to Southeast Asia, this snake genus contains the 'true cobras' as opposed to look-alikes like the king cobra — which genus?
Naja is a genus of venomous elapid snakes commonly known as cobras (or "true cobras").
What's the name for the scholarly study and collection of coins, paper money, tokens and medals — though by its rules, cigarettes traded in prison don't count?
Numismatics is the study or collection of currency, including coins, tokens, paper money, medals, and related objects.
Inflammation of the enzyme-and-hormone-producing organ behind the stomach, it comes in acute and chronic forms and can lead to diabetes — what is this condition?
Pancreatitis is a condition characterized by inflammation of the pancreas.
This Belgian-British microbiologist helped discover the Ebola virus in 1976 and led the fight against that first recorded outbreak before becoming a pioneering AIDS researcher — who is he?
Peter Piot (born 17 February 1949) is a Belgian-British microbiologist known for his research into Ebola and AIDS.

There are only five of these convex, regular three-dimensional shapes — including the cube, tetrahedron, and icosahedron — where every face is an identical regular polygon. What are these shapes called?
Platonic solid is a convex, regular polyhedron in three-dimensional Euclidean space.
Discovered in 1915 and too faint to see with the naked eye, which small, dim star, orbiting its two brighter neighbors once every 550,000 years, is our closest stellar neighbor after the Sun?
Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
Physicists denote this stretching of light's wavelength — caused by relative motion, gravity, or cosmic expansion — with the symbol z; its opposite is called blueshift. What is it?
Redshift is an increase in the wavelength, or equivalently, a decrease in the frequency, of electromagnetic radiation (such as light).

Grown mainly from Eastern and Northern Europe into Russia, this cold-tolerant grain crop is a member of the wheat tribe and its vigorous growth suppresses weeds while providing early forage for animals — name it?
Rye (Secale cereale) is a grass grown extensively as a grain, a cover crop and a forage crop.
This Russian politician has served as mayor of Moscow since 2010, after earlier stints as a regional governor, head of the presidential administration, and deputy prime minister — who is he?
Sergey Sobyanin (born 21 June 1958) is a Russian politician, serving as the 3rd mayor of Moscow since 21 October 2010.
Known by such nicknames as 'sour dock' and 'spinach dock,' this tangy Eurasian herb thrives wild in grasslands and is often used as a leaf vegetable — which plant?
Sorrel (Rumex acetosa) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the family Polygonaceae.
The fifth most common element on Earth, this multivalent nonmetal usually turns up in sulfide and sulfate minerals and is a bright yellow crystalline solid — what is it?
Sulfur (American spelling or sulphur (Commonwealth spelling) is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.

Proposed by Albert Einstein in special and general forms published in 1905 and 1915, this framework superseded 200-year-old Newtonian mechanics and explains gravitation's relation to the other forces of nature — name it?
Theory of relativity comprises two physics theories by Albert Einstein: special relativity and general relativity. Special relativity applies to all physical phenomena in the absence of gravity.

Native only to New Zealand and resembling a lizard, this reptile is the sole surviving member of an order that was hugely diverse in the Mesozoic era, with fossils dating to the Middle Triassic — what's the animal?
Tuatara (Mori:; Sphenodon punctatus) is a species of reptile endemic to New Zealand.
This Russian-American inventor built a television system using cathode-ray tubes and worked on image tubes and the electron microscope — who was he?
Vladimir K. Zworykin (1888/1889 - July 29, 1982) was a Russian-American inventor, engineer, and pioneer of television technology.

Native to freshwater and brackish habitats across western Eurasia, this ray-finned fish in the perch family, related to perch, ruffe, and darters, has become a popular game species well beyond its original range. Name it?
Zander (Sander lucioperca), sander or pikeperch, is a species of ray-finned fish from the family Percidae (which also includes perch, ruffe and darter).
Prescribed for ADHD and narcolepsy but also misused as a euphoriant, this fixed-dose pill packs four different amphetamine salts into one tablet. What is its brand name?
Adderall: Drug mixture used mainly to treat ADHD and narcolepsy.
This Scottish physician shared the 1945 Nobel Prize for discovering penicillin, and in 1922 identified an enzyme in his own nasal discharge — who is he?
Alexander Fleming: Scottish physician and microbiologist (1881–1955)
This inorganic salt, most commonly used as a soil fertilizer, is 21% nitrogen and 24% sulfur by content — what is it?
Known by the symbol Sb and mined chiefly from stibnite ore, which element has long been powdered into the cosmetic kohl and today hardens lead in car batteries?
Antimony: Chemical element with atomic number 51 (Sb)
His namesake effect — scattered X-rays losing energy — proved light behaves as particles and earned a share of the 1927 Nobel Prize in Physics. Who was this American physicist?
Best known for pioneering radical behaviorism at Harvard, this psychologist invented a chamber for studying operant conditioning that came to bear his name — who is he?
B. F. Skinner: American psychologist and social philosopher (1904–1990)
Originating in the Swiss Alps' canton of Bern, this large farm breed historically pulled carts for alpine herders and traces its ancestry to Roman mastiffs — which breed, recognized in 1912?
Bernese Mountain Dog: Swiss breed of dog. The Bernese Mountain Dog, German: Berner Sennenhund or Dürrbächler, is a large dog breed originating from the canton of Bern, Switzerland and the Swiss Alps.
The only trijet ever produced by its manufacturer, this airliner entered service with Eastern Air Lines in 1964 powered by three rear-mounted turbofans?
A tree-like cluster of dark-green flower heads sprouting from a thick pale stalk, this cabbage-family vegetable is a close cousin of cauliflower and can be eaten raw or cooked — what is it?
Broccoli: Edible green plant in the cabbage family.
Named to honor the Virgin Mary and her golden crown, this daisy-family flower is also known as the pot marigold — which plant?
Calendula officinalis: Species of flowering plant in the daisy family Asteraceae.
Its Greek-derived genus name Xylocopa literally means 'wood-cutter,' fitting for an insect that burrows nesting tunnels into dead wood or bamboo — which insect is it?
Carpenter bee: Common name for a genus of bees.
India's third lunar mission carried a lander named Vikram and a rover, both replacing equivalents lost when the previous mission crashed on landing. What was the rover called?

Chandrayaan-3 is the third mission in ISRO's Chandrayaan lunar-exploration programme, consisting of the lander Vikram and the rover Pragyan, replacements for the equivalents on Chandrayaan-2, which crashed on landing.
In this chronic liver condition, healthy tissue is replaced by scar tissue and regenerative nodules, choking blood flow and causing portal hypertension — what is it called?
Cirrhosis: Chronic disease of the liver, characterized by fibrosis.
In this prolonged state of deep unconsciousness, a person cannot be awakened, shows no normal sleep-wake cycle, and may even be induced deliberately during general anesthesia — what is it?
Coma: State of unconsciousness. The person may experience respiratory and circulatory problems due to the body's inability to maintain normal bodily functions.
Smelling of vanilla but tasting bitter, which plant compound isn't itself an anticoagulant, though its derivatives inspired the blood-thinning drug warfarin?
This Zambian-born economist turned heads with four New York Times bestsellers, including "Dead Aid," which argues that foreign aid actually holds Africa back. Which author and life peer is it?
Dambisa Moyo, Baroness Moyo: Zambian-born economist (born February 1969)
Known for feigning death when cornered, which genus of cat-sized marsupials includes the only marsupial species found north of Mexico?
Didelphis: Genus of marsupials. The six species in the genus Didelphis, commonly known as Large American opossums, are members of the opossum order, Didelphimorphia.
Nicknamed 'Viking disease,' this hand condition — first surgically treated in 1831 by the surgeon it's named after — permanently curls the ring finger inward. What is it?
Dupuytren's contracture: Medical condition featuring permanent bending of fingers.
A Swedish scientist and inventor until, at 53, dreams and visions sent him into a spiritual phase, this polymath became best known for his 1758 book on the afterlife, Heaven and Hell — who was he?
Emanuel Swedenborg: Swedish scientist, philosopher, and theologian (1688–1772)
With a sweet smell like pear drops, this colorless solvent turns up in nail-polish remover and is used to decaffeinate tea and coffee. What is it?
Named after a 19th-century English physicist, this SI unit measures a material's ability to store electrical charge, equal to one coulomb per volt — what is it?
Farad: SI unit of electric capacitance.
Patented in 1962 and sold under a brand name synonymous with 'roofies,' this benzodiazepine is notoriously linked to date-rape drug use — what is it?
Flunitrazepam: Benzodiazepine sedative. Flunitrazepam, sold under the brand name Rohypnol among others, is a benzodiazepine used to treat severe insomnia and assist with anesthesia.
Born in Pisa in 1564, this Italian polymath has been crowned the father of observational astronomy and the scientific method — and was among the earliest tinkerers to build a thermoscope. Who is he?
Galileo Galilei: Italian physicist and astronomer (1564–1642)

This Italian friar and cosmological theorist proposed that stars were distant suns with their own planets, and was tried for heresy by the Roman Inquisition for insisting the universe is infinite — who was he?
Giordano Bruno: Italian Dominican friar, philosopher and mathematician (1548–1600)

After proving a 20-year-old open problem in Riemannian geometry known as the soul conjecture, this reclusive Russian mathematician later quit the field entirely and now lives in seclusion in Saint Petersburg — who is he?
Grown as deciduous shrubs across the temperate Northern Hemisphere and related to the birch family, this plant produces a popular round brown nut — which plant genus?
This branch of biology studies the microscopic structure of tissues, historically distinguished from cytology (the study of cells) and organology (the study of organs) — what is it called?
Histology: Study of the microscopic anatomy of cells and tissues of plants and animals.
This nearly worldwide genus of flowering plants — commonly called St. John's wort — was the subject of a definitive taxonomic monograph identifying 36 sections within it. Which genus?
Hypericum: Genus of flowering plants known as St. John's worts.
This Belgian-American physicist-mathematician is best known for wavelets that revolutionized image compression — a family of them even bears her name; who is she?
Ingrid Daubechies: Belgian physicist and mathematician (born 1954)
Working under Tamerlane around 1400, this Persian astronomer and mathematician produced work that mostly never reached Europe and stays largely unpublished — who is it?
Jamshid al-Kashi: Persian astronomer and mathematician (c. 1380–1429)
Fluent in Quechua after being raised in two Indigenous households as a child, this Peruvian novelist and anthropologist became known for his intimate portrayals of Andean culture — who is he?
Caused by a thiamine deficiency often linked to heavy alcohol use, this brain disorder is marked by amnesia and confabulation, and frequently pairs with Wernicke encephalopathy — which condition?
Korsakoff syndrome: Mental illness caused by a lack of thiamine in the brain.
This Turing Award winner brought order to the chaos of distributed computing — and, on the side, created the document-preparation system LaTeX and wrote its first manual. Who is he?
Leslie Lamport: American computer scientist and mathematician (born 1941)
Reaching about 200 kg at its largest, this reddish-brown-shelled reptile ranges through the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans as well as the Mediterranean — which species?
Loggerhead sea turtle: Species of marine reptile distributed throughout the world.
Also called the dorado or common dolphinfish, this surface-dwelling ray-finned fish is found around the Gulf of Mexico, Costa Rica, and Hawaii — what is it?
Mahi-mahi: Species of fish. It is also widely called dorado (not to be confused with Salminus brasiliensis, a freshwater fish) and dolphin (not to be confused with the aquatic mammal dolphin).
This German physicist won the 1914 Nobel for discovering how crystals diffract X-rays, then — a fierce opponent of Nazism — helped rebuild German science after the war. Who is he?
Originally known as amethopterin, this chemotherapy drug also treats autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, and can end ectopic pregnancies — what is it?

Flown by the Imperial Japanese Navy from 1940 to 1945 and code-named 'Zeke' by the Allies, this long-range carrier fighter combined agility, speed, and firepower unmatched early in WWII — which aircraft?
Mitsubishi A6M Zero: Japanese carrier-based fighter aircraft. The A6M was designated as the Mitsubishi Navy Type 0 carrier fighter (零式艦上戦闘機, rei-shiki-kanjō-sentōki), or the Mitsubishi A6M Rei-sen.
Taking its name from the Latin for 'weasel,' this is the largest family in the suborder Caniformia — gathering otters, badgers, martens, and wolverines under one roof. What is it?
This group of three genetic conditions causes nervous-system tumors; its first type brings café au lait skin spots and scoliosis, while its second causes early hearing loss — what's it called?
Neurofibromatosis: Three genetic disorders involving benign tumors of the nervous system.
This condition of involuntary eye movement can be triggered by stimulating the ear's semicircular canals — for example with the caloric test — while the head stays still. What is it?
Nystagmus: Dysfunction of eye movement. Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.
A playful, fish-eating cousin of weasels and badgers, this semiaquatic mammal is known for sliding down natural slides and toying with stones — what is it?

He joined the British Astronomical Association at age 11, compiled the Caldwell catalogue, and hosted the BBC's "The Sky at Night" — the longest-running TV series with its original presenter. Who was this English amateur astronomer?
Patrick Moore: English astronomer, broadcaster and writer (1923–2012)
Structurally related to a calming brain chemical and acting like baclofen or GHB on the same receptor, this anxiety medication can also give a mild dopamine-driven lift at low doses — what is it?

Often at its worst with the very first steps of the day, this common foot disorder inflames the connective tissue supporting the arch and is linked to tight calf muscles and heel spurs — what condition is it?

Plantar fasciitis: Connective tissue disorder of the heel. Plantar fasciitis or plantar heel pain is a disorder of the plantar fascia, which is the connective tissue that supports the arch of the foot.
Sold under the brand name Lyrica, this anticonvulsant amino-acid drug also treats fibromyalgia, nerve pain, and anxiety — which medication is it?
Pregabalin: Anticonvulsant medication. Its use in epilepsy is as an add-on therapy for partial seizures.
Named by the medieval scholar Gerard of Cremona, this black-looking opening in the eye's iris is round in humans but a vertical slit in cats and a horizontal bar in goats — what is it?
Pupil: Part of an eye. The pupil is a hole located in the center of the iris of the eye that allows light to strike the retina.

A canine native to the southeastern United States, intermediate in size between the coyote and gray wolf. For a century its status as a separate species has been debated — some call it a coywolf. Name this animal.
Red wolf: Canid native to the southeastern United States. Fish and Wildlife Service recognizes the red wolf as an endangered species and grants it protected status.

He dreamed up an "impossible" triangle, traded ideas with M. C. Escher, and shared the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics for proving black holes are a robust prediction of general relativity — who is this English mathematician?
Roger Penrose: English mathematician, mathematical physicist (born 1931)
This Taiwanese-American physicist shared the 1976 Nobel Prize with Burton Richter for discovering the subatomic J/ψ particle. Who is he?
Samuel C. C. Ting: Nobel prize winning physicist.
The sole living species in its genus, this coastal California evergreen is the tallest tree species on Earth, reaching over 116 meters and living 2,200 years or more. What is it?
Sequoia sempervirens: Species of tree. Sequoia sempervirens is the sole living species of the genus Sequoia in the cypress family Cupressaceae (formerly treated in Taxodiaceae).

Named in 1842 from Brazilian fossils and often called a saber-toothed tiger despite no close kinship to true tigers, this genus of prehistoric predator roamed the Americas until the early Holocene — which animal?
Smilodon: Extinct genus of saber-toothed cat.
It's the largest order of reptiles — lizards and snakes alike — set apart by horny scales they periodically shed and a hinged upper jaw that lets snakes gape around big prey. Which order?
Squamata: Order of reptiles. The now-extinct mosasaurs reached lengths over 14 m (46 ft).
This tangy reddish spice, made from a shrub in the cashew family, is a staple of Arab cuisine and holds symbolic significance on the Haft-sin table at Persian New Year — what is it?
Sumac: Related species of plants in the family Anacardiaceae.
Prized for its durability and water resistance, this tropical hardwood with a leather-like smell when freshly milled is a top choice for boat building — what is it?
Teak: Tree species native to South and Southeast Asia.
In the standard anatomical position, this is the outermost digit of the hand, right next to the index finger — which digit, known in Latin as the pollex?
Thumb: First digit of the hand. When a person is standing in the medical anatomical position (where the palm is facing to the front), the thumb is the outermost digit.
Known as a noxious weed for its spiky, woody burs that can puncture bare feet and even bicycle tires, this invasive desert-loving plant is native to Eurasia and Africa — name the species?
Tribulus terrestris: Species of flowering plant. Tribulus terrestris is an annual plant in the caltrop family (Zygophyllaceae) widely distributed around the world.
This hormone-responsive organ nourishes a developing embryo and fetus until birth, connecting at its narrow lower end to the cervix and at its upper corners to the fallopian tubes — what is it?
Uterus: Female sex organ in mammals.
Usually appearing on the hands and feet due to a human papillomavirus infection, this benign skin growth typically clears on its own within months to years — what is this common growth called?
Wart: Small, rough growth resembling a cauliflower or a solid blister.
One of Europe's largest bee species, this dark, iridescent carpenter bee nests in dead wood and is generally not aggressive unless provoked — which insect?
Xylocopa violacea: Species of bee. Xylocopa violacea, the violet carpenter bee, is the common European species of carpenter bee, and one of the largest bees in Europe.

The symbol for krypton is Kr. Krypton is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

In what year was Dwayne Johnson born?
Dwayne Johnson: Dwayne Douglas Johnson (born May 2, 1972), also known by his ring name "The Rock", is an American actor and professional wrestler.
In what year was Jude Law born?
Jude Law: David Jude Heyworth Law (born 29 December 1972) is an English actor.
In what year was Chris Evans born?
Chris Evans (actor): Christopher Robert Evans (born June 13, 1981) is an American actor.
In what year was Ryan Gosling born?
Ryan Gosling: Ryan Thomas Gosling ( GOSS-ling; born November 12, 1980) is a Canadian actor.
In what year was Rooney Mara born?
Rooney Mara: Patricia Rooney Mara ( MAIR-ə; born April 17, 1985) is an American actress.

Sophie Turner: Sophie Belinda Turner (born 21 February 1996) is a British actress.

Aaron Paul (born Aaron Paul Sturtevant; August 27, 1979) is an American actor.
In what year was Julian Sands born?
Julian Sands: Julian Richard Morley Sands (4 January 1958 – c. 13 January 2023) was an English actor.
In what year was Hulk Hogan born?
